Encryption.//: PROD-57: evidence and reports encrypted at rest. The key is protected by CertificateThumbprint if set, else by the integrity certificate (chain key's, else signing) or the CyberArk chain key. Nothing is encrypted until a backup exists: RecoveryCertificates (.cer files, public part only; their private keys offline) or shares from casebook-keytool split. Losing the key loses the encrypted files: read OPERATIONS.md section 2 (Evidence key) first.

Config.//: CAP-16: a folder of public keys (PEM) whose configuration bundles import here without a typed key id, besides this server's own; for example the test server's, exported from its Integrity page. Blank = none. Read at startup; a file that isn't an RSA key stops it.

SigningKey.//: F-23: where the seal signing key comes from. File (the PEM at SigningKeyPath), CertificateStore (CertificateThumbprint in LocalMachine\My; the app account needs read on its private key) or CyberArk (Secret = an @cyberark:Safe=...;Object=... reference to the PEM). Retired public keys for rotation go in RetiredPublicKeysPath (blank = a 'retired' folder beside SigningKeyPath). See OPERATIONS.md section 2.

ChainKey.//: F-25: hash the audit chain with a secret key (HMAC-SHA256) so database access alone can't rewrite recent history. OFF by default, and one-way in practice: keyed entries can only be checked while their key is held, so back the key up first. Source CyberArk (Secret = an @cyberark: reference to 32 random bytes, base64; earlier keys in RetiredSecrets) or Certificate (CertificateThumbprint; the key is generated once and kept encrypted at WrappedKeyPath, earlier ones in RetiredWrappedKeysPath). See OPERATIONS.md section 2.

SealCopies.//: F-27: optional extra copies of each seal, each off while blank. EmailTo: addresses for a seal digest (a mailbox under retention; needs email on in-app). TimestampAuthorityUrl: an INTERNAL RFC 3161 timestamp authority (only private addresses are accepted); tokens are saved beside each seal in ExportPath. Seals also go to the SIEM as event 5004 whenever a SIEM transport is on. See OPERATIONS.md section 2.

EvidenceVerify.//: F-17: periodically re-hash stored evidence and alarm when bytes drift from the recorded SHA-256. Off by default (re-hashing is I/O-heavy); administered in-app. A run also happens at startup; each run checks its share of the files, every file at least every PassDays days (PROD-53).

Upgrade.//: C18/BUG-644: the one-time integrity upgrade runs in the background once the app has been up this many minutes. Keep it above the upgrade script's 11-minute warm-up, so a failed upgrade rolls back before any row is rewritten.

Security.//: F-15: minutes of inactivity before a session is locked and the live circuit is torn down. 0 disables the app-level timeout. Administered in-app (Administration -> Settings -> Security); this is the fallback default.

Downloads.//: F-13: per-user token bucket on the evidence/report/export download endpoints. TokenLimit is the burst; TokensPerPeriod refill over PeriodSeconds sets the sustained rate. Over budget => immediate 429 + a SIEM event (5306). Server-side security config; restart to change.

Reporting.//: E-15: when true, a report must be approved by someone other than the analyst who generated it (two-person control). Administered in-app (Administration -> Settings -> Reporting); this is the fallback default.

Sla.//: E-16: per-severity response-time targets in hours (Detected -> Contained / Resolved). Blank/0 disables a severity's SLA. Administered in-app (Administration -> Settings -> Response SLA); these are the fallback defaults.

Compliance.//: PROD-07 / UX-15: regulatory notification-deadline clock. Off by default; the clock + per-jurisdiction rules are administered in-app on one page (Administration -> Regulatory deadlines); these are the fallback defaults.

Severity.//: Admin-configurable display labels for the fixed severity levels (level/order/colour/SLA are unchanged; the stored value is always the canonical enum). Administered in-app (Administration -> Settings -> Severity labels); these are the fallback defaults.

Access.//: C-05: read/access logging. LogScope = Off | RestrictedOnly | All. CoalesceWindowMinutes folds repeat accesses of the same case/artifact by the same user into one session. Out of the tamper-evident chain; administered in-app (Administration -> Settings -> Access logging).

DataProtection.//: Empty in dev = framework default (per-user keyring). In prod set an absolute, ACL-restricted folder so the antiforgery/circuit keyring survives app-pool recycles; keys are encrypted at rest (DPAPI machine scope).

BackupStatus.//: H-04: path to the JSON status file the out-of-band backup/restore jobs write (see docs/OPERATIONS.md §1.3). Empty = not configured (dev). Thresholds drive the Diagnostics staleness verdict.

Email.//EnableSsl: Encrypt the SMTP connection (STARTTLS). Server-side only; default true. Set false only for a relay that terminates TLS itself (e.g. a trusted localhost submission agent).
Email.//SmtpSignIn: CAP-05: blank = the sign-in set in Administration (Settings -> Notifications -> Email sign-in), else none. Set here, it wins: SmtpUsername + SmtpPassword (@protected:, @cyberark: or a literal), or SmtpUseDefaultCredentials (the app-pool account). Not both.
Email.//AssignmentNotifications: E-03b: email a person when they are assigned to a case. Admin-editable (Settings → Notifications). Off by default.

Notifications.//: E-03b: the periodic overdue after-action scan emails each item owner (else the case's incident commander) a reminder, once per item. Read-only over case data; sends only when Email:Enabled. Admin-editable (Settings → Notifications). Off by default.
Notifications.//DueSoonScan: E-03d: the periodic due-soon scan reminds each item owner (else the case's incident commander) once ahead of the deadline, when an item is due within LeadHours. Fires before the item lapses; the overdue scan still catches it if it does. Read-only; sends only when Email:Enabled. Admin-editable (Settings → Notifications). Off by default.
Notifications.//DeadlineScan: PROD-37: the periodic regulatory notification-deadline scan reminds a case's incident commander + assignees once as its deadline crosses into at-risk, and again if it passes. Also requires the deadline clock on (Compliance:NotificationDeadlines:Enabled); read-only and never mutates case state — a human still records the reported milestone. Sends only when Email:Enabled. Admin-editable (Settings → Notifications). Off by default.
Notifications.//StaleScan: PROD-38: the periodic stale-case nudge reminds a case's incident commander + assignees once when an open case has had no recorded activity (any audited case work) for longer than its severity's threshold in Days; a new activity re-arms it. Read-only and never mutates case state. Sends only when Email:Enabled. Admin-editable (Settings → Notifications). Off by default; a Days value of 0 disables the nudge for that severity.
Notifications.//DigestScan: PROD-39: the consolidated work digest sends each opted-in user one grouped email of their open follow-up items (overdue / due today / due this week) on the cadence they chose (account menu → Notifications). This is the master switch (off by default) — a user gets a digest only when this is on AND they've opted in to Daily or Weekly. Read-only; never mutates case state. Sends only when Email:Enabled. Admin-editable (Settings → Notifications).
Notifications.//Mandatory: PROD-16: personal notification types the organization enforces — users cannot opt out of a mandatory type (their per-user opt-down under the account menu is ignored for it). The compliance breach→Legal distribution is always sent regardless. All off by default, so users may tune assignment / overdue / due-soon emails for themselves.
Notifications.//Chat: PROD-02: which notification types are also broadcast to the team chat channel (Slack/Teams). Requires Chat:Webhook configured on the host. Admin-editable (Settings → Notifications). All off by default.

App.//: E-03b: absolute base URL of this deployment (e.g. https://casebook.corp.example), used to build direct links and the logo in notification emails. Admin-editable (Settings → Notifications). Blank = emails omit links and the hosted logo (they still render, branded, with a text wordmark).

Agenda.//: E-39: signing secret for the per-user agenda calendar (ICS) subscription feed (/agenda/feed.ics?token=...). Server-side only (a bearer secret, like the seal signing key) — NOT admin-editable. Blank = the subscribable feed is disabled (the authenticated one-shot download /agenda/agenda.ics still works). Set a long random value in appsettings.Production.json to enable Outlook subscriptions; rotating it invalidates every issued feed URL.

Siem.//: F-18: outbound security-event stream to SIEM. Transports (webhook JSON, syslog CEF) fan out from a bounded queue. Endpoints/secret stay in server-side config (not the in-app editable settings); status is shown read-only in Admin. Both transports disabled by default.

Webhook.//: JSON POST to the SIEM HTTP Collector. AuthHeader/AuthScheme match the collector (Authorization: Bearer, or x-api-key). Token may be a literal or, with Secrets:CyberArk enabled (F-19), a reference like '@cyberark:Safe=SIEM;Object=CaseBook-Webhook-Token' fetched from CyberArk CCP at runtime, or a @protected: value. CAP-40: leave Token blank to enter it in Administration (Integrations, SIEM webhook token, encrypted with Data Protection); set here, it wins. A token that won't resolve or decrypt stops the send rather than sending without it.

Syslog.//: CEF over syslog to an SIEM Broker VM / syslog collector. Protocol Udp (fire-and-forget), Tcp or Tls (CAP-33: RFC 5425, usually port 6514; the collector certificate must be trusted and issued to Host; optional ServerCertificateThumbprint pin and ClientCertificateThumbprint in LocalMachine\My). Facility 16 = local0.

EventLog.//: Windows Event Log (Windows hosts only). Register the source once, as an administrator, before enabling: New-EventLog -LogName Application -Source CaseBook.

Chat.//: PROD-02: outbound team-chat notification channel (Slack/Teams incoming webhook), a broadcast alongside email. The webhook URL is the channel credential, so it stays in server-side config (not the in-app catalog) and shows read-only in Admin → Server configuration. Which notification types post here is chosen in-app under Notifications:Chat. Disabled by default; https-only egress.

Webhook.//: WebhookUrl is the Slack Incoming Webhook URL or a Teams channel connector/workflow URL. It may be a literal or, with Secrets:CyberArk enabled (F-19), a reference like '@cyberark:Safe=SOC;Object=CaseBook-Chat-Webhook', or a @protected: value. CAP-40: leave WebhookUrl blank to enter it in Administration (Settings, Notifications, Team chat webhook, encrypted with Data Protection); set here, it wins. Format: Slack (mrkdwn text) or Teams (MessageCard).

Updates.//: PROD-49: the update check. CheckEnabled and CheckIntervalHours are admin-editable (Administration -> Updates); Repository and Proxy stay server-side. One anonymous GET to api.github.com; nothing about the installation is sent. Off by default.

Secrets.//: F-19: optional secret retrieval from CyberArk CCP. When CyberArk:Enabled=true, any config secret written as a reference ('@cyberark:Safe=<safe>;Object=<object>') is fetched from the Central Credential Provider at runtime instead of being stored here. Literal values are used as-is (opt-in per secret). CCP authenticates this app by client certificate and/or allow-listed machine/OS-user; no CCP password is stored. Disabled by default.
